comment: What a paid plan counts and charges by use, as DATA (decision source:cnVuLXlvdXItYnVzaW5lc3Mtc3RvcmFnZS1hd2FyZS1wcmljaW5nLTIwMjYtMTAtMDM, Avery 2026-10-03: pricing must include storage; a flat plan loses money on someone keeping 18 TB; Avery 2026-10-05: $100/month per spot plus the actual usage plus a small margin, or Trillion goes bankrupt, decision source:cHJpY2luZy1hbmQtYmlsbGluZy11c2FnZS1zcG90cy1iaWxsaW5nLXNjcmVlbi1zZXR0aW5ncy0yMDI2LTEwLTA1). A meter names the `reading` its count comes from (a reading the person's store answers by name, src/person-store.mjs usageReadings: stored-bytes, work-cost; a new reading is one reader there and then any meter row can use it), how many of the read amount make one `unit` (`per_unit`), how many daily counts make one `per` of its price (`days_per`: 30 for a level kept each day and priced by the month, 1 for an amount used that day and priced per unit), the provider's `event_name` its daily count is sent under, and where its price comes from: `cost.records` reads every record of that kind at `path`, takes the `take` of them (highest: what the most expensive place Trillion keeps it costs), or `cost.unit_dollars` sets the listed base rate when the unit itself is a share of measured row usage; either way the price is that base rate times `margin`, rounded up to `round_up_cents` (a whole cent when absent) per unit per `per`. The work meter uses published marginal row rates before Cloudflare monthly allowances, so its base rate is not the provider invoice. Tests ensure prices stay above the configured base rates. `shown` says how a person reads an amount: `scale` turns units into the shown number, `before` and `after` go around it, `digits` how many places. An offer row names the meters it charges by in its own `usage` rows ({ meter, included, price_option_id, currency }): `included` units come with the plan and only what is above them is charged, counted once a day while the plan is paid for (a free trial is not charged). A usage row may name its own `margin` (a price experiment's arm testing the margin), which replaces the meter's for that offer and is never below 1, so no offer charges below its configured base rate. A subscription bought before an offer carried a usage row keeps what it bought until its next renewal (src/payment.mjs startPlanUsage), and each paying account's store sends its counts once a day through the operator account's `tool` (src/plan-usage.mjs). Adding a metered resource is one row here and one usage row on an offer: AI apps as paid members, like people, are one reader (the apps connected that day) and one row with its price, put on the offers that sell them. Team seats (offer:trillion-team, not for sale) carry no usage row, so a seat holder's files are not counted. Each agreement keeps its last `history_days` counted days (readings by name) so Billing can draw them. A meter's `words` may name `{cost}` (the listed base rate for one unit) and `{margin}`, and `words.included_none` is said instead of `words.included` when a plan includes none of it, so a plan says plainly that it charges the listed base rate plus the margin, with both numbers (Avery 2026-10-05).
_retry_minutes: How long a policy owner waits to count a day again after its count failed (src/account-control.mjs countPlanUsage); the day is kept and never counted twice (src/plan-usage.mjs).
_ledger_days: How many days of an account's priced settled work its quota owner keeps (src/resource-budget-owner.mjs resource_budget_ledger, with the day's budget usage and holds): longer than any report waits, so an account no plan counts still keeps a bounded ledger; a payer's acknowledged days go sooner.
_permit_retention_hours: How many hours a settled permit, its events and observations are kept after it settled (src/resource-budget-owner.mjs pruneSettled): longer than a command is retried (minutes) or its stored result erased; a permit an account erasure holds is kept. Hours, not days: one account settles 600,000 a day at about 5 KB each, so a week of them overran the 10 GB store. The accounting it settled into (usage, days) is not touched.
_settle_prune_slack_minutes: How long past permit_retention_hours a settled permit or event may sit before a settle prunes it: the quota object's alarm prunes at the retention itself, so a settle finds nothing and writes nothing, and prunes only after an alarm was missed.
_service_key_scrub_days: How many days the service-actor key an earlier version stored is kept, once the account has a derived one (src/derived-keys.mjs), to check claims it signed; claims are made again on use, so it is dropped after this.
_permit_prune: How the quota object's alarm and its full-store recovery take off settled permits past that retention: alarm_pages pages of alarm_page permits (and as many events) per turn with yield_ms between them so a waiting call runs, another turn continue_ms (longer than a turn) later while old ones remain, a check every check_minutes otherwise, retry_ms after a turn that threw (the alarm keeps retention, so a settle seldom prunes).
